title: Websites and Web Apps
tagline: A website that still works well a year from now.
summary: Company websites, online shops, customer portals and internal tools, built so they stay fast and stay easy to change.
problem: Most websites are judged on how they look in the first week. The real bill arrives later. Pages that felt quick with fifty customers crawl with fifty thousand. A small change turns into a week of work. The one person who knew how to update it has moved on, and nobody else can. None of this is visible on launch day, which is why it keeps happening to good businesses.
outcomes: A site that stays quick as your business grows
Changes that take hours instead of weeks
Something any competent developer can pick up later, so you are never stuck with one person
A safe way to undo a change if something goes wrong

whatWeDo.title: Company and marketing websites
whatWeDo.description: The site your customers judge you by. Fast to load on a phone, easy for your team to update without calling a developer, and built so search engines can read it properly.

whatWeDo.title: Customer portals and dashboards
whatWeDo.description: The place your customers log in to see their account, their orders or their data. This is where most of the real work sits, and where most of the mistakes get made.

whatWeDo.title: Internal tools
whatWeDo.description: The screens your own staff use every day. Usually the least glamorous part of a business and the one where a few hours of work saves someone a few hours a week, forever.

whatWeDo.title: Online shops
whatWeDo.description: Product pages, carts and checkout. We put extra care into payment, because that is the part where a small fault costs real money and nobody notices for days.

whatWeDo.title: Speed and search
whatWeDo.description: Pages that load quickly on an ordinary phone on an ordinary connection, and that search engines can index cleanly. Both are measured before we call anything finished.

whatWeDo.title: Moving an existing site
whatWeDo.description: If your current site sits on something that no longer fits, we move it across in stages, with the old one running until the new one is proven. No weekend where everything is switched at once and hoped for.

whatYouGet: Everything we build, owned by you, in your own accounts from the first day
Written instructions any developer can follow, so you are never dependent on us
A way to publish changes and undo them in one step
Checks that run automatically before anything reaches your customers
A site people can use with a keyboard or a screen reader
whatsNotIncluded: Logo design, brand identity or naming
Writing your marketing copy, though we will tell you where the words are doing the heavy lifting
Paid advertising and search marketing campaigns
Desktop software you install on a computer
timeline: Usually six to twelve weeks, agreed after a first conversation

process.title: Understand the job
process.description: What the site has to do, who uses it, and what already exists. If a smaller version would answer your question faster and cheaper, we say so now rather than after you have paid.

process.title: Agree the plan
process.description: A written plan covering what we will build, what we will not, how long it takes, and the risks we can already see. You approve it before any work starts.

process.title: Build in small pieces
process.description: Every week you get a working version on a private link and a short written update. You watch it take shape instead of waiting for a reveal at the end.

process.title: Make it solid
process.description: Speed checks, accessibility checks, backups, and a tested way to undo a bad change. This is part of the work, not a step that gets dropped when the date gets close.

process.title: Hand it over
process.description: Written instructions, a walkthrough with whoever takes it on, and everything transferred into your accounts. Leaving us should never be difficult.

seo.title: Websites and Web Apps
seo.description: Company websites, customer portals, internal tools and online shops. Built to stay fast and easy to change, and owned by you from day one.

title: Online Products
tagline: From a first version to something a real business can run on.
summary: Subscription products and platforms, including the accounts, payments, permissions and behind the scenes work a product needs once paying customers arrive.
problem: Getting a first version working is the easy half. What breaks a young product is everything the demo never needed. A second customer whose information must never be visible to the first. A failed card payment that quietly leaves an account switched on. A task that fails at three in the morning and tells nobody. A support question your team cannot answer because there is no screen that shows them the answer. Nobody asks for any of this, and it decides whether the product survives its first hundred customers.
outcomes: Each customer's information kept properly separate from every other customer's
Payments and access that stay in step, including when a card fails or someone cancels
Automatic work that tells someone when it fails, instead of failing quietly
A screen your own team can use to answer customer questions, without asking a developer

whatWeDo.title: First working version
whatWeDo.description: The smallest version that answers the real question, built so version two is not a fresh start. Where we take a shortcut, we tell you it is a shortcut and what it will cost to undo.

whatWeDo.title: Accounts and permissions
whatWeDo.description: Signing in, teams, and who is allowed to see what. Built to hold up when your first large customer asks for their own rules, rather than being bolted on later.

whatWeDo.title: Payments and subscriptions
whatWeDo.description: Free trials, upgrades, downgrades, failed cards, refunds and cancellations. The unglamorous cases are the ones that lose money quietly, so they get the most attention.

whatWeDo.title: Work that runs on its own
whatWeDo.description: Scheduled reports, reminders, imports and anything that talks to another company's system. Set up so that when something fails, a person is told and it can be run again safely.

whatWeDo.title: Knowing what is happening
whatWeDo.description: Alerts when something breaks, and a small set of numbers worth watching. Set up to reach a person, not to sit on a screen nobody opens.

whatWeDo.title: Handling growth
whatWeDo.description: Finding the specific thing that is actually slow and fixing it, rather than paying for a bigger server and hoping the problem goes away.

whatYouGet: A product a team other than ours can run and keep building on
Written instructions for the problems that are likely, not the ones that are interesting
An admin screen for the questions your support team will really get
Alerts that have been tested, not just switched on
A written record of the decisions that would be expensive to reverse, and why we made them
whatsNotIncluded: Market research, pricing strategy or launch marketing
Round the clock emergency cover, unless it is agreed separately
Anything that needs a licence or certification we do not hold
timeline: Three to six months to a first release, then ongoing

process.title: Understand the problem
process.description: What the product must do, for whom, and what has to be true for it to be worth building. We push back here if the plan is bigger than the question it answers.

process.title: Agree the shape
process.description: How the product will be put together and which decisions would be expensive to change later. Those get written down with the reasoning, so nobody has to guess in a year.

process.title: Build the foundation first
process.description: Accounts, payments, permissions and publishing before features. Adding any of them to a working product later costs several times more than starting with them.

process.title: Build features weekly
process.description: A working version every week on a private link, planned together and adjusted as you learn from real customers.

process.title: Keep it running
process.description: Alerts, written instructions, and either a handover to your team or ongoing support from us. Both are fine, and we tell you which one we think suits you.

seo.title: Online Products
seo.description: Subscription products and platforms, including accounts, payments, permissions and support tooling. From a first release to something a business can run on.

title: Mobile Apps
tagline: An app that works on the train, not only on office wifi.
summary: Apps for iPhone and Android, built once and released to both, including the parts most teams forget until the reviews arrive.
problem: Phones punish assumptions that a website forgives. The signal drops halfway through saving something. A customer is two versions behind and will never update. A rejected release costs a week of waiting. A fault you released is live until Apple approves the fix. Teams who treat an app as a website in a smaller window find all of this out afterwards, from their star ratings.
outcomes: A clear answer to what happens with no signal, instead of a spinning circle
Older versions that keep working for the customers who never update
Releases that anyone on your team can publish, not just one person on one laptop
Crash reports that point at the real cause

whatWeDo.title: One app, both phones
whatWeDo.description: Built once and released to both iPhone and Android, which keeps the cost and the ongoing work far lower than building the same app twice.

whatWeDo.title: Working without a signal
whatWeDo.description: What the app does on a train or in a lift, and what happens to anything saved while offline. Decided at the start, because it cannot be added neatly afterwards.

whatWeDo.title: Keeping older versions working
whatWeDo.description: A meaningful number of your customers will not update for months. The app keeps working for them while you keep releasing for everyone else.

whatWeDo.title: Notifications and links
whatWeDo.description: Push notifications handled properly on both phones, including when someone refuses permission, and links that open the right screen even from a cold start.

whatWeDo.title: Releasing
whatWeDo.description: Test versions your team can install, releases rolled out gradually so a fault reaches few people, and small fixes that can go out without waiting for approval.

whatWeDo.title: Getting through the app stores
whatWeDo.description: Store listings, screenshots, privacy declarations and the review process. We have read the rules so you do not have to, and we budget time for the rejection that sometimes comes.

whatYouGet: The app published under your own Apple and Google accounts, never ours
Every key and certificate handed over securely
A release process written down so anyone on your team can run it
Crash reports that point at the real cause
The store listing material both companies require
whatsNotIncluded: Games or heavy three dimensional graphics
Rebuilding an existing app separately for each phone
App store advertising and paid installs
Software for physical devices and hardware
timeline: Two to four months to the first store release

process.title: Answer four questions
process.description: Which phones, how old a phone we support, what has to work without a signal, and which phone features you genuinely need. These four answers decide most of the cost.

process.title: Build the foundation
process.description: Moving between screens, saving information on the phone, and how the app talks to your system. The offline rule is settled now, not later.

process.title: Test on real phones
process.description: A test version every week on actual devices. Simulators on a developer's computer hide slowness and hide every permission prompt.

process.title: Prepare the release
process.description: Store listings, screenshots, privacy declarations and submission, with time set aside for a rejection.

process.title: After launch
process.description: Watch the crash reports, release gradually, and ship the first fix. There is always a first fix.

seo.title: Mobile Apps
seo.description: Apps for iPhone and Android built once and released to both, including offline behaviour, notifications, releases and app store submission.

title: Rescue and Support
tagline: Take on the software nobody wants to touch.
summary: For software that already exists and has become risky to run. We check it, tell you plainly what is wrong, fix what matters, and keep it working.
problem: Working software and safe software are two different things, and the gap only shows up on the worst possible day. When we look inside software built in a hurry, we usually find the same handful of problems. The passwords to the system are sitting somewhere anyone who looks can find them. There is no backup, or there is one that nobody has ever tried to restore. Faults happen and nobody is told. The people who built it were not careless. They were working fast, with tools that never mention which parts are missing.
outcomes: A plain English report on what is actually wrong and what each problem would cost you
The passwords to your system changed and properly hidden
Backups that work, which you have watched being restored
Someone told when something breaks, before your customers notice

whatWeDo.title: A full check
whatWeDo.description: Three to five days going through everything, including the history of every change ever made, which is where old passwords tend to hide. It ends in a written report with every problem rated by how serious it is, and an hour on a call going through it with you.

whatWeDo.title: Fixing what matters
whatWeDo.description: Passwords changed and hidden properly. The lock moved to the right side of the door. Backups switched on and restored in front of you. Alerts wired up so a person is told. Out of date parts brought up to date carefully. A tested way to undo a bad change.

whatWeDo.title: Ongoing support
whatWeDo.description: Security updates on a schedule, backups tested rather than assumed, someone watching for faults so you are not the one who finds them, and a short written report each month. This is what stops everything drifting back.

whatWeDo.title: Writing it all down
whatWeDo.description: Most software we take on has no instructions at all. We write them as we go, so how it works is not trapped inside whoever touched it last.

whatWeDo.title: Taking over from someone who left
whatWeDo.description: Where the original developer or agency is gone, we work out how everything fits together by reading it, then take responsibility for it.

whatWeDo.title: Building on it again
whatWeDo.description: Once it is stable and we know it properly, we can add to it. We will not add features to software we have not read.

whatYouGet: A written report with a plain English summary at the front for whoever is not technical
Every problem rated by how serious it is, with the real world consequence spelled out
A list of what to fix first, ordered by risk rather than by how easy it is
Backups that work and a tested way to undo a bad change
Alerts that reach a person
whatsNotIncluded: Formal security certification. We find the obvious problems, we are not an accredited auditor.
A promise that a check finds every fault. Nobody can honestly offer that.
Selling you a patch when the honest answer is starting again. If that is the answer, we say so, even when it costs us the work.
New features before the software is safe to change
timeline: The check takes three to five days. Fixes usually take one to three weeks.

process.title: Sign a confidentiality agreement
process.description: Signed before you give us access to anything. It covers your software, your information and anything else we happen to see.

process.title: Read only access
process.description: Checking your software means reading it, not changing it. We do not ask for the ability to change anything, and we do not ask for your customers' information.

process.title: The check
process.description: Three to five days of reading. If we find something genuinely urgent, you hear about it the same hour rather than waiting for the report.

process.title: Report and walkthrough
process.description: The written report, then an hour on a call going through it. What you do next is entirely your decision. Taking the report to your own developer is a perfectly good outcome.

process.title: Fix, then keep it working
process.description: If you want us to do the work, it arrives in small pieces you can check. Your live site is untouched until you approve.

seo.title: Rescue and Support
seo.description: For software that already exists and has become risky to run. We check it, report plainly what is wrong, fix what matters and keep it working.
